lead_raw_text:
The structure of Ca2Hg2N2 (reduced formula CaHgN) crystallizes in the triclinic space group P1 (No. 1), with six atoms in the unit cell distributed over six independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis identifies Ca centers with eight geometric neighbors (six Ca and two Hg, 2.73–3.41 Å), Hg centers with five neighbors (two Ca and three N, 2.73–2.99 Å), and N centers in two- and three-coordinate environments, the latter containing one Ca and two Hg. The geometric neighbor graph forms a single three-dimensional component spanning all six sites. Validated polyhedron-sharing relations include corner and edge sharing between eight-vertex Ca polyhedra and five-vertex Hg polyhedra, plus corner and face sharing between Ca polyhedra.
